prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of proposals in the 2015 manifesto (max 500 words)

Fiscal and economy
- Raise the personal allowance to at least £13,000; introduce a 30% income tax band; lift the 40% threshold to £55,000; abolish inheritance tax; increase transferable allowance for couples to £1,500.
- Cut small-business rates by 20% for properties with rateable value under £50,000.
- Fund plans by: leaving the EU (saving net contributions), reducing overseas aid to 0.2% of GNI over three years, cancelling HS2, replacing the Barnett Formula with a needs-based system, cutting central government and quangos, and abolishing some departments by merging functions.
- Independent costing cited from an external economic consultancy.

Immigration and borders
- Leave the EU to end free movement; introduce an Australian-style points system; five-year moratorium on unskilled immigration.
- Create five visa routes (work, visitor, student, family, asylum) with medical insurance requirements for temporary migrants; increase border staff by 2,500; count people in and out; no amnesty for illegal entrants.
- Restrict access to non-urgent NHS care and most benefits until five years of contributions; faster removal of foreign offenders; revoke status obtained by fraud.

Health and social care
- Invest an extra £12bn over five years in the NHS; fund 8,000 GPs, 20,000 nurses, 3,000 midwives; GP-in-A&E pilots; free hospital parking.
- Increase mental health funding (£170m/year) and dementia research/treatment (£130m/year).
- Tackle eligibility abuse (“health tourism”); introduce manager licensing; replace Monitor/CQC with elected county health boards; end new PFI use.
- Increase social care funding by £1.2bn per year (phased), integrate health and social care under the NHS, improve home-care standards, and raise Carer’s Allowance by £572/year.

Welfare, pensions and family
- Scrap the “bedroom tax”; retain Housing Benefit for under-25s; option to pay rent direct to landlords.
- Disability assessments returned to GPs/specialists; fund 800 advisers in foodbanks.
- Flexible state pension window; boost pensions guidance; ban pension cold-calling; lifetime war widows’ pensions.
- Childcare reform: deregulate to expand places and lower costs; require primary schools to offer wraparound care 8am–6pm; more nursery provision via planning; shared parenting presumption in family courts; system-wide child protection review.

Education
- Abolish Key Stage 1 SATs; reduce teacher workload; expand grammar, vocational and technical routes; later transfer exams; reintroduce intermediate GCSE Maths; remove AS as A-level step; statutory first-aid education.
- Reverse special-school closures; refocus Ofsted on teaching and wellbeing.
- Remove tuition fees for UK students on approved STEMM degrees in return for five years’ UK work.

Housing and environment
- Build 1m homes on brownfield by 2025 via a national register, remediation grants, and first-sale stamp duty relief up to £250k; bring empty homes back into use.
- Prioritise locals in social housing; restrict access for new migrants until five years’ tax/NI.
- Channel Right-to-Buy receipts into new community housing; protect green belt; allow local referenda on major developments; make mortgages inheritable.

Transport and energy
- Cancel HS2; review southeast airport capacity; support Manston reopening; limit speed cameras to safety use; oppose road pricing/eCall; scrap DCPC; increase levy on foreign HGVs.
- Repeal the Climate Change Act; end subsidies for new onshore wind/solar; support hydro, nuclear, gas and shale (with a sovereign wealth fund); support coal with CCS; cut green levies and prepayment penalties.

Work, business and trade
- Prioritise resident workers in hiring; enforce minimum wage; code for zero-hours (no exclusivity, 12-hour notice or pay, path to secure contracts).
- Tackle late payments via HMRC sanctions; pilot government-backed trade credit insurance; 30 minutes’ free town-centre parking.
- Leave the EU; seek a bespoke UK–EU free-trade agreement; restore WTO seat; negotiate global FTAs; retain cooperation in selected European agencies.

Farming, fishing, heritage, pubs
- Replace CAP with a capped UK Single Farm Payment; support dairy/small producers; improve animal welfare, labelling, small abattoirs.
- Exit the CFP; restore a 200‑mile EEZ; reallocate quota to the under‑10m fleet; protect spawning/no‑take zones.
- Zero VAT on listed-building repairs; “seaside town status” tools; support microbreweries; permit ventilated smoking rooms; oppose alcohol minimum pricing.

Crime, justice, defence, foreign aid, governance
- Add frontline staff across police, prisons and borders; review offences/sentencing; withdraw from supranational arrest and human rights jurisdictions; UK Bill of Rights; decriminalise TV licence nonpayment; deport foreign offenders; expand prison capacity with education focus.
- Meet/exceed 2% of GDP on defence; retain nuclear deterrent; strengthen carriers; create a Director of National Intelligence; income tax exemption while on operations; build veteran housing/hostels.
- Reduce overseas aid to 0.2% GNI; focus on emergency relief, vaccinations, water/sanitation; fold DFID into the Foreign Office.
- Political reform: citizens’ initiatives, robust recall, open primaries, confirmation and expenditure hearings, proportional voting with constituency link, tighten postal voting, English-only laws voting.
